warnings: Increase inflow emission temporal sampling to avoid “per-frame stepping”: raise Flow > Sampling Substeps from 2 to ~4–8 (keep an eye on bake time).

Increase solver time-stepping stability/detail (without changing Resolution 96): raise domain max substeps/time steps (e.g., Max Substeps 6–8) and ensure adaptive time stepping is enabled so the jet doesn’t quantize into segments.

Tune liquid mesh generation so the jet doesn’t become chunky lobes: adjust liquid mesh settings (particle radius factor / smoothing / concavity) to produce a smoother, more continuous sheet/stream before breakup.

Ensure secondary spray is actually being produced *and rendered*: enable spray particles in the domain and assign renderable particle geometry/material (small spheres/instances) so micro-droplets appear around the jet edges and impact zone.

Refine the emitter to better form a fan: keep plane_init true, but adjust emitter plane aspect and orientation/spread so it starts as a thin sheet that tears into ligaments (rather than a thick slug). Slightly reduce plane thickness and add small velocity variation/turbulence to break repetition.

Improve floor wet look: drive a wetness mask centered at the impact point (not global origin) and increase specular + lower roughness only where wet; add subtle concrete normal/roughness texture for scale.

Water shader: reduce blue tint (water should be near-clear in thin layers), keep IOR ~1.333, very low roughness, and rely on strong specular highlights; consider enabling caustics options if available/desired for sharper refractive highlights.
Lighting: make the overhead fluorescent more tube-like/rectangular and increase intensity contrast to get sharper, silvery-white streak highlights on the jet and puddle.
Add slight motion blur (small shutter) for fast droplets, and/or slightly stronger DOF focus on the rupture/impact zone to increase photographic realism.
